chapter_mapping: Chapter P1 Radiation and waves. L1 = P1.1 (risks and benefits of radiations), L2 = P1.2 (climate change and the evidence for it), L3 = P1.3 (how waves behave), L4 = P1.4 (light and sound meeting different materials, separate science only - correct for this qualification).
assessment_check: No lesson asserts a paper structure, so nothing needed correcting. For the record: J259 has four components - Breadth 01 (Foundation) and 03 (Higher), Depth 02 (Foundation) and 04 (Higher) - each 90 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 50% of the tier's GCSE, and both papers assess content from all teaching chapters. There is no paper 1 / paper 2 content split.
equations_check: The only P1 equation is wave speed = frequency x wavelength (spec reference P1.3.6), which sits in the recall-and-apply list and is not bold, so both tiers must recall it. The unit never claims it is given. Both worked examples and both calculation questions recompute correctly: 440 Hz x 0.77 m = 338.8 m/s; 3 Hz x 0.2 m = 0.6 m/s; (3 x 10^8) / 1500 m = 2 x 10^5 Hz.
answer_keys_check: All 20 knowledge checks re-derived, including the four matching items and their order arrays. Every key is correct; the only faults were missing tier flags. All 43 flashcard answers checked against the article and the spec; no duplicate answers within a lesson.
katex_check: No broken delimiters. All 15 KaTeX spans use \( ... \) or $$ ... $$ correctly.

findings.claim: <div class="higher-only"> wraps the whole radio-wave paragraph (n7), including 'Radio waves have the longest wavelengths and lowest frequencies', the AM/FM, television and long-range communication uses, and the diffraction-over-hills sentence.
findings.truth: Only the last sentence is Higher tier. P1.1.10 (radio waves produced by, or inducing, oscillations in electrical circuits) is the one bold statement; the groupings and their uses are P1.1.1 and P1.1.9, neither bold, so both tiers. body.tier-foundation .higher-only is display:none, so a Foundation reader opened the box and saw microwaves only - radio waves vanished from the spectrum tour.
findings.evidence: spec P1.1 outcomes 1, 9, 10 (bold file, page 17-18); css/style.css line 5062

findings.claim: Q3 'Explain why gamma rays are more dangerous than radio waves, referring to ionisation' is typed '3 marks - Explain (HT)'.
findings.truth: Both-tier content. P1.1.7c (high energy ultraviolet, gamma rays and X-rays cause ionisation) and P1.1.8 (hazardous effects on human tissue) are not bold.
findings.evidence: spec P1.1 outcomes 7c and 8, not bold

findings.claim: Q6 (L1) and Q4 (L3) are typed '4 marks - Required Practical Method'.

Retype to '4 marks - Practical Method', the label already used elsewhere in this subject. The L3 activity itself is right for the board (ripple tank, P1.3.7b, PAG4).
findings.evidence: spec chapter P8: 'OCR has split the requirements ... into eight Practical Activity Groups or PAGs'; no 'required practical' anywhere in J259

findings.claim: 'This limited frequency response is the reason human hearing has the range it does.'
findings.truth: Overstated to the point of being wrong. Human hearing runs from roughly 20 Hz to 20 kHz. The 1 kHz to 3 kHz efficiency band of the ossicles explains where hearing is most sensitive, not the width of the range. The spec asks only for the relevance of the limited range to human hearing.
findings.evidence: spec P1.4 outcome 7 and the bold P1.4 narrative (1 kHz to 3 kHz); settled fact on the audible range

findings.claim: Key Fact: 'the 1 kHz to 3 kHz range, which is the frequency range of normal speech'.
findings.truth: Speech covers a far wider band and the pitch of a speaking voice is nearer 100-250 Hz. 1-3 kHz is the band that carries most of the information needed to understand speech - which is how the paragraph above already puts it. The Key Fact is brought into line with it.
findings.evidence: settled fact on speech fundamentals; lesson paragraph n14 already states it correctly

findings.claim: In the 'Applications: Ultrasound, SONAR and Earthquake Waves' collapsible, <div class="higher-only"> sits inside collapsible-inner, so only the two paragraphs are wrapped.

findings.claim: Q4 mark scheme: 'Closer particles transfer vibrations more quickly (less energy is lost between particles), so the wave travels faster'.
findings.truth: Energy loss does not set wave speed. Absorption reduces amplitude as a wave travels; it does not slow it. The bracket teaches a misconception inside a mark scheme, where a student will copy it. The rest of the scheme (longitudinal wave, particles closer together) is the accepted GCSE reasoning and stays.
findings.evidence: settled fact: wave speed in a medium is set by the medium's properties, not by attenuation

findings.truth: P1.4.6, P1.4.7 and P1.4.8 are all bold, so all five items are Higher tier only. Every answer key is right, and KC4's key (1 kHz) matches the spec figure exactly.
findings.evidence: spec P1.4 outcomes 6, 7, 8, bold

findings.truth: Both-tier content. P1.4.2 (ray diagrams illustrating refraction at a plane surface and dispersion by a prism) is not bold, and the P1.4 narrative on different wavelengths travelling at different speeds in glass is not bold either.

findings.claim: The lesson is titled 'Wave Behaviour - Reflection, Refraction, Diffraction', and lesson 1 says long-wavelength radio waves 'can diffract over hills and buildings'.
findings.truth: Diffraction appears nowhere in J259 - not in P1, not anywhere in the spec. The body of lesson 3 does not in fact teach diffraction, which is right; only the title promises it. Titles are not edited under this brief, so this is referred up: the title over-promises against the spec. The lesson 1 sentence is true and stays as background.
findings.evidence: grep of specs/ocr/physics-b-21c-J259.md: no match for 'diffract'

findings.truth: ALARA is a real radiation-protection principle and nothing said about it is wrong, but J259 does not name it. P1.1 asks learners to evaluate risks and benefits of technologies using radiation (IaS4). Off-spec enrichment, kept.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: no match for 'ALARA' or 'as low as reasonably'

findings.claim: Feedback loops, the ice-albedo example, ice-core data and 'carbon dioxide equivalent' are taught as core material.
findings.truth: None of these is in J259. P1.2 has only two outcomes. Ice cores are named in the chemistry spec (C1.2) as a linked topic. All of it is correct science and useful for the IaS3 modelling discussion, so it stays; the (HT) flag it carried does not (F6).
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: no match for 'feedback', 'albedo', 'ice core'

findings.claim: Paragraph n21 introduces photons and the wave-particle description of light, then says 'For your GCSE, the wave model is sufficient for all the topics assessed.'
findings.truth: Photons and quantum physics are not in J259. The framing sentence is honest and correct for this board, so the passage stays as labelled enrichment.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: no match for 'photon' or 'quantum'

findings.claim: Q6 asks for a method comparing infrared emission from surfaces of different colour and texture (a Leslie cube).
findings.truth: A sound practical, but not one of this chapter's. P1.1 lists estimating the speed of microwaves in a microwave oven, investigating how radiation intensity varies with distance, and investigating absorption, transmission and reflection of EM radiation (for example UV absorption by sunscreens). Referred up rather than rewritten: replacing it means a new question and a new mark scheme.
findings.evidence: spec P1.1 Linked learning opportunities, Practical work column

findings.claim: Coverage gaps in chapter P1 across the four lessons.
findings.truth: Untaught assessable outcomes: P1.1.6 (electrons arranged at different distances from the nucleus, and arrangements changing with absorption or emission) - only the ionisation half is taught; P1.1.7b (X-rays, ultraviolet and visible light generated when electrons in atoms lose energy); P1.1.7e (infrared emitted and absorbed by molecules) is implied in lesson 2 but never stated; P1.3.8b and P1.3.8c (how to measure refraction through a prism, how to investigate reflection off a plane mirror - both PAG8) have no method anywhere in the unit; P1.4.9 (how changes in speed, frequency and wavelength are inter-related when sound crosses into another medium) is done for light only. None of the three P1.1 practicals appears. All both-tier.
findings.evidence: spec P1.1, P1.3, P1.4 assessable learning outcomes

findings.claim: 'The Sun is extremely hot and emits most of its energy as visible light and ultraviolet.'
findings.truth: Loose. The Sun's output peaks in the visible, but by energy roughly half of it arrives as infrared and only a small share as ultraviolet. This is the standard GCSE simplification and the point the lesson needs - that the Sun radiates at shorter wavelengths than the Earth - is right, so it is left alone rather than re-narrated for a marginal gain.
findings.evidence: settled fact: solar spectral distribution; spec P1.2 narrative says only that Earth's emission has a lower principal frequency than the Sun's

summary: All four lessons carried findings: 21 FIX (18 MEDIUM, 3 LOW) and 7 NOTE, with 37 surgical edits. The dominant fault is the Higher-tier wrapper, wrong in both directions in every lesson - it hid both-tier content from Foundation readers in L1 and L2, and in L2, L3 and L4 it opened below its heading or inside its collapsible, leaving Foundation readers an empty heading or an empty box. Higher content had leaked untagged into takeaways, exam tips, knowledge checks and flashcards, while three questions carried an unearned (HT). Beyond tiering: a U+0001 control character has broken the L4 takeaways heading on the live lesson; a mark scheme taught that sound is faster in solids because less energy is lost; the ear-bone frequency band was said to set the width of human hearing; and two questions used AQA 'required practical' wording on a board that uses PAGs. Every number, equation, worked example and answer key in the unit is correct. Two items referred up: six both-tier outcomes are untaught, including both P1.3 PAG8 practicals, and the L3 title promises diffraction, which is not in J259 at all.
